title: S8 separation probe from paired S4 sectors
hypothesis: An R8 coset that preserves an R8-invariant 4+4 split inherits an unordered pair of the six published S4 sectors.
findings: Each R8-invariant 4+4 split contains 144 complete R8 cosets.
Those 144 cosets divide into all 21 unordered pairs of the six S4 sectors, with four diagonal and eight mixed cosets per pair class.
Across the seven invariant splits there are 1,008 compatible incidences: 168 diagonal and 840 mixed.
For every compatible incidence, a diagonal S4 pair is equivalent to left-right coset coincidence.
The 168 left-right coincident cosets preserve zero, one, three, or seven invariant splits with multiplicities 48, 98, 21, and 1.
The six published CC, CT, CV, TT, TV, and VV octets occupy P1+P1, P1+P2, P1+P3, P2+P2, P2+P3, and P3+P3 respectively in the standard split.
boundary: This is a complete classification of the R8 cosets that decompose through an R8-invariant 4+4 split. It does not classify the remaining cosets as physical supermultiplets, prove that the 21 pair classes are inequivalent representations, or solve the full hex separation problem.
